summary: Configured GitLab Duo for the loop with files that follow the documentation. In the repository: .gitlab/duo/agent-config.yml (image, setup script, cache, network policy), .gitlab/duo/mr-review-instructions.yaml (AFAW rules for the Code Review Flow), the workspace subagent .agents/agents/afaw-reviewer.md (tools read_file and grep only, the two of the documented example), and the sources of one custom flow (duo/custom-flow.yaml, AFAW loop reporter: Flow Registry v1, writes notes only) and one custom agent (duo/custom-agent.md, AFAW auditor, read-only), which are created in the UI because the documentation describes no repository file for them. scripts/check_duo_config.py and the duo_config job in plan reject any key, tool or limit that the documentation does not name; the custom flow is also forbidden to change code or the merge request. Verified on docs.gitlab.com on 2026-10-24: custom agents (UI creation, Maintainer role, visibility, tools, invocation from the Duo sidebar), custom flows (AI > Flows, Maintainer role, service account ai-<flow>-<group> with the Developer role, triggers mention, assign, assign reviewer, merge request and work item events), the custom flow YAML schema (rejected keys name, description, product_group; only environment ambient; no model, no params.stop; AgentComponent and OneOffComponent), the Flow Registry v1 reference (Beta), triggers (Premium or Ultimate, a human must perform the action, bots cannot start a trigger), foundational flows (group switches Allow flow execution and Allow foundational flows need the top-level group Owner on GitLab.com), the Developer flow (assign, mention, Implement button, push rules for the service account, hosted runners), Code Review flow (assign @GitLabDuo, custom instructions, approval is a beta flag), Fix CI/CD Pipeline flow (manual button; no attempt cap documented), agent-config.yml keys, mr-review-instructions.yaml structure, workspace subagents (experiment, default branch only, tools list; an unavailable tool stops the session), AGENTS.md customization, and the agent tools list. Gaps reported in docs/duo.md: the top-level group gitlab-ai-hackathon belongs to the organizers, so the foundational flow switches may not be ours to change; there is no documented event after a merge, so the summary on the issue needs a person to mention the flow's service account; no attempt cap exists in Fix CI/CD Pipeline, so the cap of 3 goes to the deterministic engine in task 012; AGENTS.md section 6.1 (the LLM never executes side-effect tools) conflicts with Duo flows and is reworded in the later AGENTS.md merge request. Nothing is claimed to run until a human enables the flows and a real session is seen.
